notes:
One typescript continuation: an opening fragment followed by twenty page-and-line comments on pages 18–25. Handwritten own number - 6 - and archive number 70 are present; there is no title, date, salutation or signature. The opening continues the preceding sheet’s ‘ne sont pas’ with a cancelled mis followed by live mis en lumière. The text states ‘la référence (V 3.3.2) est vide’ and leaves the spaces after VII and SGA 5 IV unfilled; no reference numbers are supplied editorially. Body words and reference digits are typed, including their curved numeral designs. The Gr arrow and tilde and the two large marginal strokes are hand-drawn; the two detached pairs have unassigned origin.

Authorial questions and reservations are preserved in the author’s words: ‘est-ce vraiment possible sans autre hypothèse sur Z ?’; ‘linéairement’ = ‘rationnellement’ ?; ‘Il faudrait aussi une référence pour le fait que’ dim(Z_s) = dim(Z_t); ‘N’est-il pas prudent de supposer f lisse ?’; ‘Supposer X plat sur S.’; ‘hypothèses sur X ?’; ‘donner le corollaire pour NS ?’; the request for ‘références pour’ ‘essentiellement de type fini’ and ‘universellement japonais’; and ‘dommage qu’on ne donne pas de démonstration.’ The phrase ‘manque flèche’ is an instruction in the prose, not a missing diagram supplied by this edition. The quoted standard/standart and rationnelle/rationelle pairs and the literal quoted ellipsis are retained as the proposed corrections, not silently modernized.

All five explicit C doubts were inspected. The old m in démonstration is resolved; the covered reference character gains Z as its preferred candidate; e/a and the cancelled malsonnante remain uncertain. The pair after et is preserved by its high diagonal shape, and the pale pair above final e in flèche is newly retained without a punctuation or authorship claim. The long margin stroke overlaps the prefix p.24 and is anchored accordingly. H supplies description only and has no collation rows. These notes report the page’s assertions and requests; no proof or computation was performed.
math_reading_decisions: Each ordinary capital was inspected in its own occurrence on the halves: Z in the p.19 question; Z and S in the p.20 reference; both Z letters in the dimension equality; X and S in p.22; X in p.23; N and S of NS; and both final S letters. They show ordinary single typewriter outlines, not independent double strokes.

The Gr line was additionally viewed in one tight crop: both G letters have one ordinary outline, both superscripts are solid raised points, and the second term has lowered top with a descending p. The added arrow is a single rightward shaft with a wavy overscript; the loop at the head is not a second parallel shaft.
The dimension equality has dim(Z_s) = dim(Z_t): s and crossed t are separately lowered; the equality is two horizontal strokes. The page’s equality was read, not proved.
The final first S is followed by a single raised prime, then a separate pair of closing quotation strokes; the other quoted S is unprimed.

The Roman references XIV, V, VII, IV and II are typewritten ordinary capitals. No additional upper or lower rules appear around them on this page. The visible reference strings are XIV 5.1 et 5.2, V 3.3.2, VII with blank remainder, SGA 5 IV with blank remainder, EGA IV 2.8, cf. IV 2.12, and EGA II 7.1.9.

C-context targets were checked individually: cancelled mis and live mis, standard versus standart, rationnelle versus rationelle, the literal quoted ellipsis, and each overprinted character. Confirmed lexical targets have explicit decision rows even where unchanged.

The new Z alternative concerns an overprinted character in a page reference, not a changed live mathematical variable. The live number remains p.22. The initial underprint of démonstration is resolved from two low arches, not from the expected live word.
